analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers gliders as engine-free aircraft, steady descent along a straight inclined flight path, definition of glide angle via height and distance, and two force-balance relations used to determine lift and drag from measured height, distance and weight.

overview.headline: Steady glider descent links glide angle to lift and drag balance

keyPoints.point: A glider is an aircraft with no engine that descends while traveling forward
keyPoints.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyPoints.point: Steady descent follows a straight flight path inclined to the ground at the glide angle
keyPoints.quote: The glider’s flight path is a simple straight line, shown as the inclined red line in the figure.

keyPoints.point: Tangent of the glide angle equals change in height divided by distance flown
keyPoints.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyPoints.point: Lift times cosine of glide angle plus drag times sine of glide angle equals weight
keyPoints.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:

keyPoints.point: Lift times sine of glide angle equals drag times cosine of glide angle
keyPoints.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: an aircraft with no engine that loses altitude as it travels in steady descent
keyTerms.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyTerms.gloss: inclined angle between the straight flight path and the ground during steady descent
keyTerms.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: trigonometry ratio equal to change in height divided by distance flown
keyTerms.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force component that together with drag balances weight in the force equations
keyTerms.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force that balances a component of lift along the glide path
keyTerms.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: force due to gravity that balances lift and drag components in steady flight
